newsitem.title: UKRAINE: SOCCER-ATELKIN GOAL SETTLES UKRAINIAN CUP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ATELKIN GOAL SETTLES UKRAINIAN CUP.

text.p: Shakhtar Donetsk seized on a solitary defensive error by Dnipro Dnipropetrovsk to snatch the Ukrainian Cup 1-0 on Sunday.
The final between two sides from the depressed coal and steel belt of eastern Ukraine was consolation for both as Dynamo Kiev seem set for fifth successive Ukrainian championship.

Striker Serhiy Atelkin made sure the cup would go to Donetsk for the second time in three years after a neat interception of a sloppy defensive pass on the edge of the Dnipro box. He hit the only goal in the 37th minute.
Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma, a former president of the Dnipro club, presented the trophy to their eastern rivals after a match with political overtones.
Kuchma's steelmaking hometown of Dnipropetrovsk is the base for one of the two business and political clans that dominate Ukraine's affairs. The other is based in Donetsk.

Dnipro and Shakhtar -- the name means "Miner" -- packed 30,000 fans into Kiev's Olympic stadium. Both enjoyed some success in the Russian-dominated days of Soviet soccer. Shakhtar won the Soviet Cup four times. Dnipro twice won the league, in 1983 and 1988.
But neither has been able to break the strangehold of twice European Cup Winners' Cup holders Dynamo Kiev on the the post-Soviet Ukrainian league.
